explanation.value: Instead of searching from each query, start a single breadth-first search with every 'D' cell in the initial frontier at distance 0. BFS expands in rounds of equal distance, so the first time it reaches a cell it has found the distance to the nearest store. Blocked cells are never entered, and cells never reached keep -1. After the BFS, each query is a constant-time lookup.

explanation.value: Allocate dist of size rows*cols filled with -1. Seed the frontier with every 'D' index at distance 0. Pop with a head index, compute row and column, and for each in-bounds neighbour that is unvisited and not 'X', set its distance and append it. Finally map each query [r, c] to dist[r*cols+c].

value: A BFS per query (the reference) costs O(area) per query and is too slow for many queries.
Multi-source BFS costs O(area) once, plus O(1) per query, but stores a full distance array.
Flattening cells to r*cols+c indices saves memory compared with tuples.
